newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal signs three pct public sector wage deal.
newsitem.headline: Portugal signs three pct public sector wage deal.

text.p: Portugal's Socialist government on Tuesday signed a three percent wage deal with one of three public sector unions, but the other two rejected the accord.
"The rise is three percent," Assistant Minister to the Prime Minister Jorge Coelho, who led the government negotiating team, told journalists.
The wage increase will be applied to all the country's 500,000 public sector employees from January 1.
Leaders of the Communist-led Common Front and the Union of Technical Staff, which refused to sign the wage pact with the government, said they would be consulting members about what action to take.

The Common Front had threatened to strike unless the government agreed to wage rises of at least 4.5 percent to bring the minimum base salary in the public sector into line with the national minimum wage.

But the government said there was little room for manoeuvre on public sector wages because of the need to keep a firm lid on inflation next year to meet economic entry tests for the European Union's planned single currency.

Independent economists viewed three percent as maximum the government could afford to pay the public sector -- which sets the pace for private sector wage negotiations -- if the inflation target of 2.5 percent for next year was not to be put at risk.
